newsitem.title: INDIA: India coalition partners, ally demand leader quit.
newsitem.headline: India coalition partners, ally demand leader quit.

text.p: The main ally of Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's coalition on Wednesday joined leftwing parties in demanding the resignation of an alliance leader accused of corruption.

The Congress party lined up with leftwing members of the 15-party United Front coalition to call for the resignation of Janata Dal party chief Laloo Prasad Yadav, who is also chief minister of the northern state of Bihar.

"We think that it is advisable for the chief minister to voluntarily resign to carry on the best democratic traditions and give a good message to the country," a Congress spokesman told a news conference.
Bihar's governor on Tuesday authorised the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to pursue legal proceedings against Yadav in a $280 million corruption scandal over animal welfare funds.

Yadav, who is president of Gujral's Janata Dal party, says he is innocent and has repeatedly rejected demands that he resign from either post. The Janata Dal is the largest party in the fractious United Front coalition.
Another alliance member, the Communist Party of India (CPI), said it would launch a mass protest to press for Yadav's resignation.
"The Janata Dal should elect a new leader and Laloo Yadav should act responsibly and step down," CPI leader Atul Anjan told Reuters.
United Front officials said they expected the alliance's decision-making Steering Committee to seek Yadav's resignation at a meeting on June 27.

The scandal dates back to the 1980s and involved the alleged siphoning off of funds for animal welfare projects. It broke last year when officials discovered large withdrawals from animal welfare accounts.
All India Radio said the governor's decision to allow the prosecution of Yadav had pushed the prime minister's party, already riven by bitter squabbling over a leadership election, into crisis.
Laloo's rival in the leadership race, Sharad Yadav, told Reuters: "As long as he was not charged, nobody defended him as much as I did.
"But now that sanction to prosecute him has been granted, he must resign to preserve the values of the movement of which we are both products," said Yadav, who is unrelated to the chief minister.
Newspapers said Gujral was in a quandary.

"Mr Gujral will now be required to do a tightrope walk for, on the one hand, he is besieged by demands for Laloo Prasad Yadav's resignation and on the other, the Janata Dal leadership cannot crack the whip, considering Mr Yadav's standing both as a mass leader and being the Janata Dal president," the Times of India said.
